# David Weng — Developer Tools (Full Reference)

> Agent-friendly CLI tools, desktop apps, a Steam Deck plugin, a browser extension, and a personal finance backend. All open-source, all single-binary where possible.

## Projects

### canvas-cli
50+ commands for Canvas LMS — courses, assignments, submissions, grading, and more.
- Docs: https://thedavidweng.github.io/site/canvas-cli/
- GitHub: https://github.com/thedavidweng/canvas-cli
- Authentication: OAuth2 token via canvas-cli auth
- JSON output: --json flag on all commands
- Safety: --dry-run, --confirm on mutations
- Key commands: courses list, assignments list, submissions list, grade, enroll

### zenodo-cli
Record management, file upload, and full InvenioRDM API access for Zenodo.
- Docs: https://thedavidweng.github.io/site/zenodo-cli/
- GitHub: https://github.com/thedavidweng/zenodo-cli
- Authentication: API token via zenodo-cli auth
- Capabilities: records, deposits, files, communities, grants
- Safety: read-only default, --confirm on uploads

### monarchmoney-cli
Accounts, transactions, budgets, and cashflow from your terminal.
- Docs: https://thedavidweng.github.io/site/monarchmoney-cli/
- GitHub: https://github.com/thedavidweng/monarchmoney-cli
- Authentication: session token via monarchmoney-cli auth
- JSON output: --json flag, versioned JSON envelope
- Key commands: accounts list, transactions list, budgets list, cashflow

### flickr-cli
Photo management, backup, upload, albums, and full Flickr API access.
- Docs: https://thedavidweng.github.io/site/flickr-cli/
- GitHub: https://github.com/thedavidweng/flickr-cli
- Authentication: OAuth1 via flickr-cli auth
- Capabilities: photos, albums, galleries, favorites, backup, upload
- Piwigo import: migrate from Flickr to self-hosted Piwigo
- Safety: --dry-run on bulk operations

### qualtrics-cli
Agent-friendly CLI for Qualtrics XM Platform & offline survey compiler.
- Docs: https://thedavidweng.github.io/site/qualtrics-cli/
- GitHub: https://github.com/thedavidweng/qualtrics-cli
- Authentication: API token via qualtrics auth
- Capabilities: surveys, definitions, async response export/import, distributions, contacts, webhooks, raw API
- Offline QSF: compile Markdown survey specs to .qsf without API credentials
- Safety: --read-only, --dry-run, --confirm gates

### tg-drive
Turn a Telegram channel into a recoverable, scriptable file tree. Ships as the td CLI and the td-gui desktop app.
- Site: https://thedavidweng.github.io/tg-drive/
- Docs: https://github.com/thedavidweng/tg-drive/tree/main/docs/guides
- GitHub: https://github.com/thedavidweng/tg-drive
- Install (CLI): brew install --cask thedavidweng/tap/tg-drive
- Desktop app: Wails v3 (Go + web frontend), same engine as the CLI; drive browser, transfers, Saved Messages import, maintenance
- Authentication: MTProto user login via td auth login
- Capabilities: virtual file tree (ls, tree, cp, mv, rm), disaster recovery (scan --full), Saved Messages import
- Storage: Telegram messages as source of truth, local SQLite cache
- Safety: operation locks, DB transactions, --confirm on mutations

### money
Local-first, self-hostable personal finance backend for AI agents and power users.
- Docs: https://thedavidweng.github.io/site/money/
- GitHub: https://github.com/thedavidweng/money
- Agent JSON: https://thedavidweng.github.io/site/money/agent.json
- Install: brew install --cask thedavidweng/tap/money
- Go install: go install github.com/thedavidweng/money/cmd/money@latest
- Features: encrypted SQLite, BYOK providers (Plaid, Bridge), stable JSON contracts, CLI-first, demo mode
- Key commands: accounts list, transactions list, transactions search, categories list, tags list, recurring list, link, sync, setup, doctor, demo
- License: Apache 2.0

## Desktop Apps

### OpenKara
Cross-platform desktop karaoke app. On-device stem separation, synced lyrics, live mixing.
- Site: https://thedavidweng.github.io/OpenKara/
- GitHub: https://github.com/thedavidweng/OpenKara
- Built with: Tauri (Rust + web frontend)
- Platforms: macOS, Windows, Linux
- Features: 2- or 4-stem AI separation (Demucs), live stem mixing, synced lyrics (LRC, embedded, CD+G), portable self-contained library

### Sukiru
Native macOS app that checks and repairs coding agents' skill libraries.
- Site: https://thedavidweng.github.io/sukiru/
- GitHub: https://github.com/thedavidweng/sukiru
- Install: brew install --cask thedavidweng/tap/sukiru
- Requires: macOS 14 Sonoma or later on Apple silicon
- Features: health checks for stale lock records, broken links, diverged copies, and skills claimed by both installers; one-click fixes routed to the owning installer (npx skills or gh skill); snapshot/rollback for every batch; skill search and install
- Privacy: no accounts, analytics, or telemetry

### Apple Say
Native macOS speech synthesis and timed text.
- Site: https://thedavidweng.github.io/apple-say/
- GitHub: https://github.com/thedavidweng/apple-say
- Install: brew install --cask thedavidweng/tap/apple-say
- Requires: macOS 14 Sonoma or later
- Features: Plain Text, LRC, and Enhanced LRC (word-level) with automatic rate scaling; System Voice, Siri Natural, and Personal Voice; export AAC, AIFF, WAV, or CAF
- Privacy: fully local, no network calls or telemetry

### SDF Flash GUI
Cross-platform desktop front end for MakeMKV's sdftool. Dump, flash, and recover MT1959 (LG and ASUS) Blu-ray drive firmware.
- Site: https://thedavidweng.github.io/sdf-flash-gui/
- GitHub: https://github.com/thedavidweng/sdf-flash-gui
- Install: brew install --cask thedavidweng/tap/sdf-flash-gui
- Built with: Rust and egui; the site embeds the real UI compiled to WebAssembly with simulated drives
- Platforms: macOS, Windows, Linux
- Safety: MT1959-only platform check, form-factor cross-flash acknowledgement, SHA-256 firmware identity, exclusive flash modes, typed confirmation, dry-run
- Features: drive probe, firmware dump, flash with progress, boot-token recovery, sdf.bin parser, sdftool or makemkvcon backends, argv-only backend calls
- License: GPL-2.0-or-later

## Plugins

### DeckPad
Decky Loader plugin that uses a Steam Deck as a Bluetooth game controller for a PC, phone, or tablet.
- Site: https://thedavidweng.github.io/DeckPad/
- GitHub: https://github.com/thedavidweng/DeckPad
- Install: Decky Loader, then DeckPad.zip from the latest GitHub release. Not in the Decky Plugin Store yet.
- Platforms: SteamOS (Steam Deck)
- Hosts: pairs through the host's own Bluetooth settings. Requires Bluetooth Low Energy HID over GATT. Tested on Linux, where it appears as an Xbox Wireless Controller.
- Controls sent: face buttons, bumpers, analog triggers, both sticks and stick clicks, D-pad, View, Menu. Steam button becomes Guide; Quick Access becomes Share. Rear buttons, trackpads, gyro, and rumble are not sent.
- Behavior: Controller Mode changes bluetoothd in memory and is undone when the mode turns off. It is off after a reboot. Quit combo is Menu + View + L1 + R1.
- License: BSD 3-Clause

## Extensions

### ADP Shifts
Browser extension that copies an ADP Workforce Now schedule into a Google Calendar the extension creates and owns, then keeps that calendar current.
- Site: https://adp-shifts.blahaj.uk/
- GitHub: https://github.com/thedavidweng/adp-calendar
- Install: Chrome Web Store (ADP Shifts). Automatic sync into a calendar named ADP Shifts. Export .ics is also in the toolbar popup.
- Userscript: Greasy Fork, ADP Schedule Export. Adds an Export .ics button on Workforce Now and does not use a Google account.
- Platforms: Chrome, Edge, Brave, Arc, and other Chromium browsers for the extension. The userscript needs Tampermonkey, Violentmonkey, or another userscript manager.
- Sync: checks daily and when Workforce Now is open. Runs when the last successful sync is more than three and a half days old. Sync now updates immediately.
- Scope: Google calendar.app.created only. It cannot read or change any other calendar. Past shifts are not rewritten.
- Privacy: no servers and no analytics. The extension uses the existing ADP session and never asks for the ADP password. Disconnect revokes Google access and erases local data.
- License: MIT

## Design Principles

- Agent-friendly — stable JSON output, predictable exit codes, distinct stdout/stderr
- Safety first — --read-only, --dry-run, --confirm gates on mutations
- Single binary — no runtime, no containers, no dependencies
- Cross-platform — Linux, macOS, Windows (amd64/arm64)
- Homebrew distribution — brew install --cask thedavidweng/tap/<tool>
